en: Hannad ibn as-Sari narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Haywah ibn Shurayh, who said: I heard Rabi'ah ibn Yazid ad-Dimashqi saying: Abu Idris 'A'idhullah informed me, saying: I heard Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani saying: I came to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, we are in the land of a people from the People of the Book; may we eat from their utensils? And it is a land of game where I hunt with my bow and hunt with my trained hound or with my untrained hound. Inform me what of that is lawful for us.' He said: 'As for what you mentioned that you are in the land of a people from the People of the Book and eat from their utensils: if you find other than their utensils, do not eat from them; but if you do not find others, wash them and eat from them. And as for what you mentioned that you are in a land of game: whatever game you catch with your bow, mention the name of Allah and eat; whatever you catch with your trained hound, mention the name of Allah and eat; and whatever you catch with your untrained hound and reach it in time to slaughter it, then eat.'

Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us: 'Asim reported to us, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about hunting. He said: 'When you shoot your arrow, mention the name of Allah; and if you find that it has killed the game, eat, unless you find that it has fallen into water, for you do not know whether the water killed it or your arrow.'

Al-Walid ibn Shuja' as-Sakuni narrated to me: 'Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from 'Asim, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said to me: 'When you release your hound, mention the name of Allah. If it catches game for you and you reach it while it is alive, slaughter it. If you reach it and it has killed it but not eaten from it, then eat it. But if you find another hound along with your hound and it has been killed, do not eat, for you do not know which of them killed it. And when you shoot your arrow, mention the name of Allah. If it disappears from your sight for a day and you find nothing on it except the mark of your arrow, eat if you wish; but if you find it drowned in water, do not eat.'

Muhammad ibn al-Walid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of that.

Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq: ash-Sha'bi narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Adi ibn Hatim—who was our neighbor, ally, and guard at an-Nahrayn—narrate that he asked the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), saying: 'I release my hound and find another hound with my hound having caught game, and I do not know which of them caught it.' He said: 'Do not eat, for you only mentioned the name of Allah over your hound and did not mention it over the other.'
And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: 'Isa ibn Yunus reported to us: Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us with this chain of transmission.

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Zakariyya narrated to us, from 'Amir, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about game struck by a featherless arrow (mi'rad). He said: 'Whatever it strikes with its sharp edge, eat it; and whatever it strikes with its broadside is killed by a blunt force (waqidh).' And I asked him about game caught by a hound. He said: 'Whatever it holds for you and does not eat from, eat it, for its slaughtering is its catching. But if you find another hound near it and fear that it took part in catching it with it and killed it, do not eat; for you only mentioned the name of Allah over your hound and did not mention it over the other.'

Abu Bakr ibn Nafi' al-'Abdi narrated to me: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Abi as-Safar narrated to us—and Shu'bah mentioned people from ash-Sha'bi, who said: I heard 'Adi ibn Hatim say: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the featherless arrow (mi'rad)... with the like of that.

Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us; he said: and Shu'bah informed me, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi as-Safar, who said: I heard ash-Sha'bi saying: I heard 'Adi ibn Hatim saying: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the featherless arrow (mi'rad)... and he mentioned the like of it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: my father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn Abi as-Safar, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the featherless arrow (mi'rad). He said: 'If it strikes with its edge, then eat; but if it strikes with its broadside and kills, then it is struck dead by blunt trauma (waqidh), so do not eat.' And I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) about the hound. He said: 'When you release your hound and mention the name of Allah, eat; but if it eats from it, do not eat, for it only caught it for itself.' I said: 'What if I find another hound with my hound and do not know which of them caught it?' He said: 'Do not eat, for you only mentioned the name of Allah over your hound and did not mention it over the other.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Bayan, from ash-Sha'bi, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), saying: 'We are a people who hunt with these hounds.' He said: 'When you release your trained hounds and mention the name of Allah over them, eat of what they catch for you, even if they have killed it, unless the hound eats from it. For if it eats from it, do not eat, as I fear that it caught it only for itself. And if other hounds mix with them, do not eat.'

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: Jarir reported to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, from 'Adi ibn Hatim, who said: I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I release trained hounds and they catch game for me, and I mention the name of Allah over it.' He said: 'When you release your trained hound and mention the name of Allah over it, eat.' I said: 'Even if they kill it?' He said: 'Even if they kill it, so long as no hound that was not with them joins them.' I said to him: 'I shoot game with a featherless arrow (mi'rad) and strike it.' He said: 'When you shoot with a featherless arrow and it pierces, eat it; but if it strikes it with its broadside, do not eat it.'

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated it to me: 'Abd as-Samad ibn 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), the like of it, except that he said: 'he would not enter.'

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to me: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hammam, from Ishaq ibn 'Abdullah ibn Abi Talhah, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) would not come to his family by night unannounced; rather, he would come to them in the morning or in the evening.

'Abdullah ibn Maslamah ibn Qa'nab, Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, Abu Mus'ab az-Zuhri, Mansur ibn Abi Muzahim, and Qutaybah ibn Sa'id all narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to us; (Second Chain) and Yahya ibn Yahya at-Tamimi—and the wording is his—narrated to us, saying: I said to Malik: Did Sumayy narrate to you, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Travel is a portion of torment; it deprives one of you of his sleep, his food, and his drink. So when one of you has fulfilled his purpose from his journey, let him hasten back to his family.' He said: 'Yes.'

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: 'Abd al-'Aziz—meaning Ibn Muhammad—narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'When you travel during times of fertile abundance, give the camels their share of the land; and when you travel during times of drought, hasten with them while they retain their marrow (energy); and when you stop for rest at the end of the night, avoid the road, for it is the pathway of animals and the shelter of vermin and pests by night.'

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'When you travel during times of fertile abundance, give the camels their share of the land; and when you travel during times of drought, quicken their pace; and when you stop for rest at night, avoid the road, for it is the shelter of vermin and pests by night.'

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Hushaym reported to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu 'Uthman, from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'The people of the West will not cease to remain triumphant upon the truth until the Hour is established.'

Ahmad ibn 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to me: my paternal uncle 'Abdullah ibn Wahb narrated to us: 'Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us: Yazid ibn Abi Habib narrated to me: 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Shumāsah al-Mahri narrated to me, saying: I was with Maslamah ibn Mukhallad, and with him was 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As. 'Abdullah said: 'The Hour will not be established except upon the worst of creation; they are worse than the people of the Pre-Islamic Period of Ignorance (Jahiliyyah); they will not supplicate Allah for anything except that He rejects it back upon them.' While they were discussing that, 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir came along, so Maslamah said to him: 'O 'Uqbah, listen to what 'Abdullah is saying.' 'Uqbah said: 'He knows best; as for me, I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: "A group from my nation will not cease to fight upon the command of Allah, overcoming their enemies, unharmed by those who oppose them, until the Hour comes upon them while they remain in that state."' 'Abdullah said: 'Yes. Then Allah will send a breeze like the scent of musk, whose touch feels like the touch of silk, leaving no soul that has within its heart even the weight of a grain of faith but that it takes its life. Then the worst of people will remain, and upon them the Hour will be established.'

Harun ibn 'Abdullah and Hajjaj ibn ash-Sha'ir narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abu az-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abdullah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say: 'A group of my nation will not cease fighting upon the truth, triumphant until the Day of Resurrection.'

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Jabir ibn Samurah, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: 'This religion will never cease to stand firm, with a band of Muslims fighting for it until the Hour is established.'

And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated it to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us: Isma'il narrated to me, from Qays, who said: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) say... exactly like the hadith of Marwan.
